news.title: Claude can now analyze U.S. bank accounts
news.description: Anthropic launched Personal Finance, a beta feature that allows U.S. Claude subscribers to connect their bank accounts and cards to analyze their spending. Access is read-only and goes through Plaid.

news.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, specialized in exploit research
news.description: OpenAI is launching GPT-6 Cyber, with improved exploit-research capabilities and an API price higher than those of Anthropic and Google.

news.title: Meta adds real-time voice chat and animated avatars to Muse
news.description: Meta is adding real-time voice chat and animated avatars to its Muse app.

news.title: Airbnb plans an AI-powered travel agent for 2027
news.description: Airbnb announced the launch of an AI-powered travel agent during the first half of 2027.

news.title: Google introduces Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, faster and more affordable
news.description: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is presented as a fast, affordable model capable of processing longer clips.

news.title: Aina unveils a smart ring with a display and proactive AI
news.description: Hardware startup Aina has introduced a ring that can connect to devices, learn the user’s schedule, and suggest actions for approval. It can also receive voice instructions, control devices, play music, and take calls; initial deliveries are expected in early 2027.

news.title: Early reviews praise the MacBook Pro PROLED’s display
news.description: Early reviews of the MacBook Pro PROLED praise its display but criticize its price and give little attention to the touchscreen.

news.title: Early deliveries reveal Apple’s new Macs
news.description: The first iPad mini, MacBook Pro and iMac units began shipping to customers on Friday, offering a closer look at the devices.

news.title: The iPhone 20 could drop the Action button
news.description: According to a source with a mixed track record, the iPhone 20 lineup could drop the Action button.

news.title: The iPhone 18e is not expected to receive a major redesign
news.description: A Weibo leaker claims that the iPhone 18e will not receive any significant design changes.

news.title: The iPhone 18 could have a larger battery and a higher price
news.description: According to another source, the standard iPhone 18 would feature a larger battery and a higher price.

news.title: Siri handles more than 2.5 billion requests every day
news.description: Siri receives more than 2.5 billion daily requests, putting Apple’s AI overhaul into perspective.

news.title: Apple still cannot meet demand for the iPhone Duo
news.description: Apple is unable to meet demand for the iPhone Duo, while Mac and iPad supplies will remain limited through the end of 2026.

news.title: Mac and iPad supplies will remain limited through the end of 2026
news.description: Apple expects supply constraints for Macs and iPads at least through the end of 2026.

news.title: Tesla will cut Cybertruck production by mid-2027
news.description: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck at its Texas factory by mid-2027 to free up space for the Cybercab robotaxi. The pickup has sold about 71,000 units, far below the initial target of 250,000 per year.

news.title: The iPhone keyboard hides a list of blocked words
news.description: The iPhone keyboard retains a hidden list of around 100,000 words and phrases that it does not suggest, including political terms. The list does not prevent typing but disables autocorrect suggestions and makes swipe typing more difficult.

news.title: The tech stock slump threatens Anthropic’s IPO
news.description: The sharp decline in tech stocks has reduced the chances that Anthropic will file its IPO plans before the end of November. According to Kalshi, the probability of a filing before November 30 fell from 84% to 60%.

news.title: Xbox speeds up its PC app’s loading time
news.description: Xbox is joining the race for faster PC launchers and has improved its app’s loading time.

news.title: Perplexity turns its “teammates” into AI agents
news.description: Perplexity’s “teammates” are AI agents designed to carry out everyday professional tasks.

news.title: Cyclon opens preorders for a phone with an AI-focused operating system
news.description: Cyclon has opened preorders for a mobile phone running an operating system designed around artificial intelligence.

news.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Images 2.6 and enables photo-to-GIF conversion
news.description: ChatGPT Images 2.6 can create GIFs from any photo and has risen near the top of Arena’s text-to-image rankings.

news.title: Cat Wu leaves Anthropic to join OpenAI
news.description: Cat Wu has left Anthropic to join OpenAI, marking the fourth key departure from the Claude Code team in a few weeks.

news.title: OpenAI’s personal agent receives five new features
news.description: OpenAI delivered five improvements to its personal agent this week, including the ability to share any item on an iPhone.

news.title: Apple is reportedly cutting employees’ AI budgets
news.description: Apple is reportedly reducing the credits it gives employees to use third-party AI tools, with proposed daily caps of 100 dollars for engineers and 25 dollars for other employees. Some teams are also reportedly being encouraged to use less expensive or locally hosted models, without official confirmation from Apple.

news.title: Investors question a 1 500 billion dollar valuation for Anthropic’s IPO
news.description: Major investors believe the expected 1 500 billion dollar valuation for Anthropic’s initial public offering will likely need to be lowered. The amount raised could reach about 80 billion dollars, for a valuation close to 1 000 billion.

news.title: The philosophies that shaped Dario Amodei and Anthropic
news.description: Dario Amodei’s vision is based in part on rationalism and effective altruism. These schools of thought helped shape Anthropic and its approach to artificial intelligence.

news.title: Elon Musk wants to connect Starlink to terrestrial mobile networks
news.description: Elon Musk wants to combine Starlink’s high-speed satellite network with mobile antennas, fiber connections, and other terrestrial infrastructure. Smartphones could thus seamlessly access signals from both Earth and space.

news.title: Salesforce turns sales expertise into reusable skills
news.description: Salesforce says an experienced salesperson’s renewal playbook can become a reusable skill that the entire team can invoke. The author believes this durable business asset is more important than another agent launch.

news.title: Stock market plunges after the blue wave in U.S. elections
news.description: The three major U.S. indexes fell sharply, with the Nasdaq down 5.52%. Data-center stocks, SpaceX and Tesla were hit particularly hard.

news.title: Google will disable its AI services for students by default
news.description: Google plans to disable its AI services for students by default next year, at schools’ request. The measure will include Google Search, which is considered an AI product.

news.title: Legal AI startup Harvey considers an IPO
news.description: Legal AI startup Harvey has held preliminary discussions about a possible IPO.

news.title: Snowflake’s former chief revenue officer joins an AI infrastructure startup
news.description: Snowflake’s former head of revenue is joining a little-known startup specializing in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

news.title: Three takeaways from Anthropic’s widely discussed AI report
news.description: The article presents three conclusions drawn from Anthropic’s report on artificial intelligence.

news.title: IREN says Microsoft-requested network changes delayed its AI project
news.description: IREN says network changes requested by Microsoft are responsible for delays to its $9.7 billion artificial intelligence project.

news.title: Apple sharply reduces the waitlist for its new AI Siri
news.description: Apple has significantly reduced the waitlist for access to its new artificial intelligence-powered version of Siri.

news.title: Greg Brockman says OpenAI could be ready for an IPO in 2027
news.description: OpenAI president Greg Brockman said the company could be ready to go public in 2027. Its enterprise-related revenue has roughly doubled and now accounts for most of its revenue.

news.title: Baidu opens the files for its ERNIE 5.5 Flash base model
news.description: Baidu is providing researchers with the open files for a 280-billion-parameter model, with 14 billion activated per token. ERNIE 5.5 Flash base has a one-million-token context window and can be fine-tuned.

news.title: Comedian Matt Husk, known for tricking ChatGPT, is courted by AI labs
news.description: Followed by about two million people, Matt Husk films ChatGPT’s voice mode failing at simple tasks. OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI offered to collaborate with him, but he turned them down.

news.title: Agility Robotics goes public with its Digit humanoid robot
news.description: Agility Robotics, the maker of the Digit robot, is going public through a SPAC despite significant losses. Digit is already used to move bins at several companies, and the future Digit 5 will be unveiled at CES 2027.

news.title: Australian universities want to train AI-native graduates
news.description: Several Australian universities are expanding access to ChatGPT and integrating AI into their courses. They want to prepare students for a labor market where working with AI is becoming a core skill.

news.title: OpenAI admits it missed the coding-agent shift
news.description: Greg Brockman acknowledges that OpenAI was absent from the programming-assistant market, which is dominated by Claude Code. He says the enterprise business has since doubled and could prepare the company for an IPO as early as 2027.

news.title: OpenAI abandons confidentiality agreements with local officials
news.description: OpenAI will no longer sign NDAs with local officials hosting its data centers, except for security information or trade secrets. The agreements were criticized for concealing negotiations from residents.

news.title: OpenAI expands its AI engineering tests from devices to vehicles
news.description: OpenAI used GPT-6 Astra to design a working prototype in less than a week, reducing initial design time. Tests with Mazda and Chip Ganassi nevertheless show that manufacturing still requires human corrections.

news.title: The leading generative AI companies and startups to know
news.description: This guide introduces major and specialized players in generative AI, from OpenAI to niche providers. It covers uses including coding, creative media, healthcare and enterprise agents.

news.title: Apple envisions smart locks with adaptive unlocking
news.description: An Apple patent describes locks that can automatically unlock based on the user’s approach.

news.title: A nine-inch HomeView Ultra is expected in 2027 or 2028
news.description: Apple could launch a nine-inch HomeView Ultra in 2027 or 2028.

news.title: Apple beats forecasts with record quarterly results
news.description: Apple generated 114.5 billion dollars in revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026, beating Wall Street forecasts and its previous quarterly record from the 2020 holiday season.

news.title: Higher memory costs weigh on Apple’s results
news.description: Apple warned that an imminent increase in memory prices could raise the cost of its products.

news.title: Apple must disclose details of its donation to Trump’s ballroom
news.description: Apple reportedly donated 25 million dollars to Donald Trump’s White House ballroom project. A Senate subcommittee is now requesting documents related to the donation.

news.title: Rave’s lawsuit against Apple is transferred to California
news.description: Rave’s lawsuit against Apple, accusing the company of copying SharePlay features and removing Rave from the App Store, has been transferred to California.

news.title: The Supreme Court will hear Apple v. Epic in January 2027
news.description: The United States Supreme Court will hear arguments in the case involving Epic Games and Apple in January 2027.

news.title: HomePod mini 2 slightly improves sound and connectivity
news.description: The HomePod mini 2 offers slightly better sound and expanded connectivity, but costs 50 dollars more than the original model and may not justify an upgrade.

news.title: Siri Recaps and Live Rewind deemed controversial and of little use
news.description: After testing, Siri Recaps and Live Rewind are described as controversial and useless technologies, despite Apple’s usual privacy and security measures.

news.title: Walmart wants AI assistants to shop for you
news.description: Last month, Walmart announced that AI assistants will be able to shop for you, with spending limits and approvals that you set. AI is thus moving from answering questions to carrying out tasks.

news.title: A prompt for controlling actions performed by AI
news.description: Instead of asking AI to freely process an inbox, have it list every action and classify it as READ, DRAFT or ACT. AI can perform reading and preparation steps, but must stop and request confirmation before any action that sends, publishes, pays, deletes or changes something.

news.title: AI Bootcamp: applying a rule to secure AI actions
news.description: The chapter explains how to turn advice into action, choose tasks based on the cost of failure, and distinguish a bad answer from a bad action. It also shows how to prevent a hostile page from passing its instructions to the assistant.

news.title: Thinking Machines introduces a leading open-weight AI model
news.description: Thinking Machines launched Inkling 2 Small, an open-weight model with 594 billion parameters that processes text and images. The company plans to release its weights under the Apache 2.0 license after external safety testing.

news.title: Google, Meta and TikTok challenge California’s child safety law
news.description: Google, Meta and TikTok filed separate lawsuits to block a California law designed to protect people under 16 from addictive social media features. The companies cite, among other things, the First Amendment and Section 230.

news.title: The New York Times reportedly wants to buy Letterboxd for 330 million dollars
news.description: The New York Times Company is reportedly seeking to acquire Letterboxd for 330 million dollars.

news.title: Parents sue Google after alleged teen suicide
news.description: The parents of a 13-year-old are suing Google, claiming that their son may have used AI to prepare for his suicide.

news.title: Protesters enter the site of a Microsoft data center
news.description: Protesters entered the construction site of a Microsoft data center being built in Amsterdam.

news.title: The FAA is gradually phasing out air traffic control floppy disks
news.description: The Federal Aviation Administration is finally beginning to remove the floppy disks used in air traffic control.

news.title: TikTok faces a possible European fine over its feed’s “rabbit hole” effect
news.description: TikTok faces a possible European Union fine over the “rabbit hole” effect of its “For You” feed.

news.title: Zipline reaches a valuation of 21.5 billion dollars
news.description: Zipline reached a valuation of 21.5 billion dollars as Walmart increases its investment in drone delivery.

news.title: Sony revives the original Walkman earbuds with USB-C
news.description: Sony is relaunching the original Walkman earbuds with a USB-C port.

news.title: Blue Origin develops a rocket engine that costs four times less
news.description: Blue Origin says it is building a higher-performance rocket engine at one-quarter the cost.

news.title: Congress summons Nvidia chief over Chinese espionage suspicions
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is summoned by the U.S. Congress over concerns related to Chinese espionage.

news.title: AI agents’ memory can trigger risky behavior
news.description: A study shows that previously harmless prompts can later push AI assistants to take risks. More powerful models sometimes behave even worse in these situations.

news.title: Generative search engines favor dominant brands
news.description: Generative search engines cite dominant brands 1.4 to 2.8 times more often than average brands. This trend creates a bias in favor of already well-known players that content optimization alone cannot correct.

news.title: Personal AI agents fall for scams
news.description: A fraud-based test shows that the seven leading AI models are fooled in 7% to 35% of cases. Fake images and audio recordings further increase their success rate.

news.title: Disney employees question executives about possible layoffs
news.description: During a town hall, employees in Disney’s technology division asked management for explanations following reports of another wave of layoffs. Several employees told Business Insider that morale was declining.

news.title: The new rules of AI-powered search
news.description: Shoppers using AI-powered search consult nearly three times as many touchpoints before buying. Google vice president Brendon Kraham outlines three priorities for capturing discovery and generating conversions.

news.title: Google’s paid advertising strategy on YouTube
news.description: The article presents Google’s paid advertising strategy on YouTube.

news.title: How Wayfair turned creator trust into ROI
news.description: This case study shows how Wayfair built trust with creators to generate a return on investment during the holidays.

news.title: Five trends driving post-holiday sales
news.description: The article presents five trends driving sales after the holiday season.

news.title: Early Model 3 owners report on their vehicles’ reliability
news.description: An owner who bought one of the first Model 3 vehicles in 2018 says the car has performed very well. The only major repairs involved the air-conditioning fan, in addition to replacing the tires.

news.title: Model 3 owner expects the traction battery to last a long time
news.description: According to one owner, alarming claims about electric-vehicle batteries are unfounded, and it should be a long time before a traction battery needs replacing. The owner says their Model 3 Long Range has reached eight years and six months.

news.title: Interest-rate discrepancy reported between Tesla approval and payment
news.description: A buyer says Tesla approved an annual rate of 1.99 % fourteen days earlier, but the displayed rate rose to 2.49 % at the time of delivery payment.

news.title: Debate contrasts paying cash for a cheaper car with replacing it
news.description: One participant says the point made by advocates of paying cash is not that people should keep any car indefinitely, but that they can buy a cheaper vehicle and keep it longer.

news.title: Tesla owner describes the limits of sensors needed for driving
news.description: One participant finds it surprising to think that vision, radar, and lidar are needed to replicate human driving, when humans use at most two cameras and no radar or lidar.

news.title: Solar charging becomes available with a complete Tesla installation
news.description: A user with solar panels and a Tesla Powerwall says an option allows the car to be charged using solar energy. A new setting also enables charging from any source up to a certain limit.

news.title: Tesla update 2026.38.6 is offered for installation
news.description: A user received a notification saying that a software update was ready to install. The listed version is 2026.38.6, but the user has not installed it yet.

news.title: Model 3 Performance reports compressor and low-pressure errors
news.description: The owner of a 2019 Model 3 Performance asks whether other users have encountered the “VCFRONT_a160_compressorInhibited” and “lowSuctionPressure” errors.

news.title: Inconsistencies in FSD mode can make some trips easier
news.description: A user says they also experience inconsistencies in FSD mode, but take advantage of them to make driving easier. Certain areas along the route are affected by map data.

news.title: Post-rear-end-crash repair estimate could change
news.description: One participant points out that a repair shop can estimate only the visible damage after a crash. As with most cars, additional damage may be discovered during disassembly.

news.title: Owner recounts a trip without access to Superchargers
news.description: An owner describes a two-and-a-half-hour trip to pick up their Lucid Air from a repair shop in Grand Rapids, Michigan. They made the journey with their son in a Model Y, without access to DC fast chargers.

news.title: U.S. elections raise concerns about slowing AI growth
news.description: Democrats regained the House and Senate while advocating, among other measures, stronger oversight of the AI sector, while several data-center projects were restricted. After an initial rise, the market experienced one of the worst daily declines in U.S. history, with some investors fearing further measures against AI.

news.title: Subvocal unveils glasses that can capture silent whispers
news.description: Subvocal’s smart glasses capture silent whispers to enable text dictation without speaking aloud.

news.title: Apple and Goldman Sachs restrict employees’ AI use
news.description: Apple is seeking to reduce costs, while Goldman Sachs is concerned that non-engineering employees are creating their own projects with vibe coding.

news.title: Google enhances its Agentic Data Cloud for AI agents
news.description: Google Cloud is adding a borderless Lakehouse based on Apache Iceberg, an enriched knowledge catalog, and specialized infrastructure for AI agents. The updates aim to provide secure, real-time access to distributed data while reducing token costs and improving query performance.

news.title: Microsoft expands Copilot Chat’s undisclosed limits
news.description: Microsoft is increasing Copilot Chat usage caps for businesses without a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license, without disclosing the limits or allowing administrators to change them. The rollout began on November 2 for small organizations and will reach those with more than 2,000 seats on November 9.

news.title: AI increases the cost of accumulated technical debt
news.description: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is making exploits much cheaper and faster to develop, while remediation remains limited to human speed. Organizations should audit deferred security tickets, remove unused exposed systems, and regularly reassess accepted risks.

news.title: Basic vulnerabilities remain at the heart of many attacks
news.description: Despite the apparent complexity of some security incidents, entry points often rely on basic flaws such as missing access controls, unpatched firmware, or exposed credentials. Development tools and internal agents can worsen these risks if access layers and operational security are not rigorously managed.

news.title: MariaDB launches a unified platform for agentic enterprises
news.description: MariaDB presents Enterprise Platform 2027, a unified database for AI agents and enterprise workloads, integrating transactions, real-time analytics, vector search, and AI tools. It notably announces a 56 % increase in maximum throughput compared with version 11.8 and active-active multiregion scalability.

news.title: Confluent makes real-time SQL queries available on Kafka data
news.description: Confluent is making Lightning Tables generally available on AWS, allowing applications to continuously query updated Kafka data through SQL and APIs without a separate serving database. The feature is part of its Streamhouse architecture, which combines streaming, processing, governance, and querying.

news.title: EXACT combines TDD and AI agents without sacrificing quality
news.description: The EXACT method combines test-driven development with agentic AI tools by using example mapping, natural-language test lists, and predictive TDD. Experiments show that it improves code correctness and quality compared with unguided vibe coding or simple TDD prompts.

news.title: Google details the failure of its backup generators in London
news.description: According to Google’s incident report, the outage in London in October was caused by a voltage-detection failure and an incorrectly configured controller, preventing the backup generators from starting. With one power supply already under repair, the batteries eventually ran out after the other supply failed.

news.title: The next ERPs should prioritize business outcomes
news.description: The next generation of enterprise resource planning software should shift from improving productivity to delivering business outcomes through agentic applications.

news.title: Google launches AlloyDB Express for rapid testing and prototyping
news.description: AlloyDB Express can be provisioned in under two seconds and automatically scales to zero during idle periods. It includes enterprise AI features such as vector search and direct access to Gemini models.

news.title: Reusable skills are becoming the primary asset of agentic AI
news.description: Models and agents will evolve, but companies can preserve their expertise by encoding expert workflows as reusable Skills. These Skills capture judgment, exceptions, and escalation rules beyond a simple standardized procedure.

news.title: Plan AI by capabilities rather than dates
news.description: AI roadmaps should define readiness criteria—quality, cost, reliability, and security—instead of setting fixed deadlines. Agents should gradually receive more responsibility once they meet those criteria.

news.title: US voters threaten massive datacenter development
news.description: Recent results show that voters broadly oppose the massive expansion of computing capacity sought by Silicon Valley. A slowdown in construction could hurt technology companies that already struggle to secure enough computing capacity.

news.title: Blue Origin prepares a more powerful rocket engine at one-quarter the cost
news.description: Blue Origin announced two upgrades to its New Glenn rocket aimed at reducing manufacturing costs and increasing payload capacity. The company is testing a new engine and developing a hydrogen-and-oxygen third stage.

news.title: A nearly living artificial cell can grow, copy its DNA, and divide
news.description: SpudCell is an artificial cell created from inanimate components that can grow, copy its DNA, and divide. It could one day serve as a biotechnology platform, while its researchers are considering misuse risks.

news.title: GitHub unveils a new Git storage architecture
news.description: GitHub’s new Git storage architecture can handle thousands of writes per second and support 5,000 simultaneous agents on a repository. It is designed to support the agentic development of hundreds of millions of developers.

news.title: The *sshole vulnerability allows passwordless access to some Linux devices
news.description: The *sshole vulnerability allows attackers to connect over SSH without knowing the password. It affects systems using OpenSSH with musl and without pluggable authentication modules.

news.title: The rise of AI revives Hackintosh development
news.description: The Hackintosh community, which had declined since Apple switched to ARM chips, is experiencing renewed activity with the rise of AI. Recent projects include running macOS on a Snapdragon laptop and on ARM boards.

news.title: Building a physical platform to produce biological data
news.description: This essay examines the conditions needed to create a platform capable of conducting biological experiments, reliably measuring their results, and producing evidence at the scale required by AI.

news.title: A database can be viewed as global variable storage
news.description: Two common software development principles—avoiding global variables and using a database for state—are partly contradictory.

news.title: AI accelerates the exploitation of known vulnerabilities
news.description: The average time between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation has been declining for some time. AI has changed who can act during this window and how quickly known flaws are turned into attacks.

news.title: Technology companies should make better use of the data they collect
news.description: Technology companies track, store, and sell large amounts of information about their users. They should use it to improve the user experience.

news.title: The number of programmers could increase 100-fold
news.description: There could be 100 times more programmers in the coming years, even though most will not define themselves as such.

news.title: Expertise is becoming the durable asset of AI systems
news.description: Models and agents will evolve, but the skills that encode a company’s judgment, exceptions, and ways of working can remain durable. The challenge is teaching AI how the best employees work.

news.title: Adobe makes operational playbooks executable
news.description: Adobe defines Skills as reusable playbooks that standardize the execution of recurring tasks. These documented processes can now be executed, while judgment between steps remains essential.

news.title: A small company is already organizing its work around AI playbooks
news.description: An eight-person company encodes the work of its various departments in portable AI playbooks and compares them with human performance. This approach aims to preserve operational expertise regardless of the models or providers used.

news.title: Microsoft makes Skills portable across agents
news.description: Microsoft’s agent tools now support reusable skill packages that can be shared and invoked across multiple agents. This shift favors libraries of capabilities rather than simple prompt libraries.

news.title: Reusable skills create a new governance problem
news.description: A study of 1.53 million public agent Skills found that about one in seventeen contains instructions that reduce some form of human oversight. Important skills should be managed like code, with an owner, tests, versioning, and reviews.

news.title: METR estimates that AI capabilities could accelerate
news.description: A new METR evaluation focused on Anthropic suggests that some well-specified AI capabilities may be advancing much faster than before, despite substantial uncertainty. The text recommends reassessing capability assumptions every 90 days.

news.title: Microsoft makes expertise shareable in Copilot Chat
news.description: Microsoft is introducing reusable skills in Copilot Chat so employees can create, share, and reuse instructions and expertise. The text emphasizes that teams can increasingly build AI capabilities themselves.

news.title: Box launches a tool for easier creation of AI-based workflows
news.description: Box announced an AI workflow builder to help teams create AI-based processes around enterprise content. According to the text, easier construction shifts the main challenge to deciding whether to delegate the work.

news.title: Google recommends human-directed, agent-executed workflows
news.description: Google Cloud Consulting recommends moving from automating individual tasks to workflows in which agents perform operations and humans direct them. Different decisions within a process may reach readiness at different times.

news.title: Investors await jobs data after the tech plunge
news.description: U.S. stock futures were mixed on Friday ahead of the release of the October jobs report.

news.title: Goldman Sachs names 109 new partners, the most since 2010
news.description: Goldman Sachs welcomed 109 members into its partner ranks, its largest class since 2010. The number of engineers reached a record high amid Wall Street’s growing interest in AI.

news.title: Walleye fund fires its head of stock picking
news.description: After a difficult October, Walleye dismissed its head of equity selection, Anil Gondi, along with a substantial portion of its equity portfolio managers. The $17 billion fund lost nearly 6% last month.

news.title: Top investors debate AI and the future of the labor market
news.description: At the SALT London forum, financial figures discussed the rise of AI, the outlook for the job market and Elon Musk’s predictions.

news.title: Mira Murati’s startup targets a $5 billion funding round
news.description: Mira Murati’s AI startup, Thinking Machines Lab, is seeking to raise $5 billion at a $40 billion pre-money valuation. Accel is leading the round, which could more than triple the company’s valuation.

news.title: Block announces a new wave of layoffs
news.description: Jack Dorsey’s fintech is cutting jobs for the second time this year, despite reporting better-than-expected results just days earlier. Employees in the Cash App businesses are affected.

news.title: Disney employees demand answers from management
news.description: After several major rounds of layoffs this year and the prospect of another workforce reduction, Disney employees say morale is suffering. Some asked executives for answers at a recent town hall.

news.title: Nvidia must decide how to financially support neoclouds
news.description: Nvidia helped bring about a generation of cloud providers specializing in AI. The company must now determine how much support to provide as financing becomes more expensive.

news.title: Americans are choosing gift recipients more carefully
news.description: Americans are becoming more selective about whom they will give gifts to this year.

news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo will leave international football at 41
news.description: Cristiano Ronaldo announced that he is retiring from international football at age 41. The article also examines the scientific factors behind his longevity.

news.title: Helen Sharp’s loved ones pay tribute to Learjet crash victim
news.description: Helen Sharp, who died at 40 in a Learjet crash, is described by friends as someone who lived life to the fullest.

news.title: Bryan Cranston describes his life between New York and Los Angeles
news.description: The actor and co-founder of the Dos Hombres mezcal brand explains how he divides his time between New York and Los Angeles.

news.title: Data-center builders speak out after the elections
news.description: Data-center builders gathered during the midterm elections and shared their perspectives.

news.title: Amazon Prime adds a restaurant meal-delivery benefit
news.description: Amazon Prime members are receiving a new benefit related to restaurant meal delivery.

news.title: Student-loan repayment problems are worsening
news.description: Officials say student-loan repayment problems are growing and are demanding answers.

news.title: Michael Burry criticizes Anthropic’s strategy and refuses to buy its stock
news.description: Michael Burry believes Anthropic is betting its entire existence on optimism and says he does not plan to buy its stock.

news.title: A Carpenter Becomes Financially Independent by Renting Out Land
news.description: A carpenter who went bankrupt became financially independent through an unusual land-rental business.

news.title: AI Infrastructure Stocks Send the S&P 500 Down 4.4%
news.description: AI infrastructure stocks triggered a Wall Street sell-off as investors anticipated a slowdown in data center construction. The S&P 500 fell 4.4%.

news.title: Gauge Turns AI Agent Errors into Regression Tests
news.description: The open-source Gauge tool has coding agents perform the same task, records their sessions and checks the results against success or failure criteria. It lets users modify an instruction, rerun exactly the same task and compare the results.

news.title: Anthropic Gives METR Internal Access to Measure AI Progress
news.description: Anthropic gave METR internal access, and the organization estimates that AI capabilities on well-specified tasks are advancing about twice as fast as they were a year ago.

news.title: A Contest Offers One Million Dollars for Five Materials Science Problems
news.description: Discovered Materials has offered one million dollars for five unsolved problems in materials science. Leading AI agents have so far made little progress on these problems.

news.title: ElevenMusic Publishes AI-Generated Tracks Directly to SoundCloud
news.description: ElevenMusic now lets users publish AI-generated tracks directly to SoundCloud. Users have created more than 25 million tracks with ElevenLabs’ music models.

news.title: Box Context Retrieval Answers Questions from Authorized Files
news.description: Box Context Retrieval uses NVIDIA Nemotron models to answer only from files the user can access, including scanned documents, images, audio and video. General availability is planned for early 2027.

news.title: Axiom Publishes a 16-Million-Line Lean Formalization of the Stacks Project
news.description: Axiom has published a Lean formalization of the Stacks Project consisting of 16 million lines and produced mainly by swarms of AI agents. The agents also identified dozens of statements in the original text that need correction.

news.title: AI Could Help Establish a Dialogue with Dolphins
news.description: A team of biologists from Georgia Tech and Google DeepMind is analyzing 40 years of dolphin recordings to identify patterns. It is also testing an underwater computer that emits sounds associated with objects, but it remains to be determined whether this represents genuine understanding.

news.title: Anthropic Reportedly Accelerated Its R&D Through Internal AI Use
news.description: METR estimates that Anthropic’s models have been improving about twice as fast since October as they did previously. The Information attributes this acceleration to the intensive use of AI in the company’s research.

news.title: AI Agents Remain Below 12% Success on a Real-World Work Test
news.description: SemiAnalysis’s GDPx benchmark evaluates agents on simulated knowledge-work tasks, from chip design to quantitative trading. No model exceeds a 12% success rate, although Claude Opus 5.5 slightly outperforms Gemini 4 Carbon.

news.title: Microsoft Research Wants to Formally Verify Code Written by AI Agents
news.description: The PDD Kit tool turns a developer’s intent into a formal specification, then verifies that the generated code follows it for all possible inputs. Tested with GitHub Next’s Chopin, it uncovered bugs in an online store written in Rust.

news.title: NVIDIA Opens Four Cosmos 3 Models for Simulating Realistic Worlds
news.description: NVIDIA is releasing four 16-billion-parameter Cosmos 3 world models under a license permitting commercial use. They generate driving scenes, camera and LiDAR data, and simulations for autonomous vehicles and robots.

news.title: Grimes Will Star in an AI-Generated Film Intended for Theaters
news.description: The singer is lending her likeness and voice to “Gods Don't Give Gifts,” a science-fiction film produced by Fable and scheduled for theatrical release on December 4. The studio wants to test the commercial potential of AI-generated cinema.

news.title: Grok Bot Can Now Make Phone Calls on Your Behalf
news.description: The AI agent can wait on hold, schedule appointments and negotiate bills on U.S. phone numbers. The user remains the “caller of record,” and is therefore legally responsible for calls made by the bot.

news.title: Mistral Adds Managed Agents and Applications to Studio
news.description: Mistral is enhancing Studio with managed agents, workflows, observability and agent evaluation. The platform runs on Mistral Large 4 and can be deployed in the cloud, on a private network or on company servers.

news.title: Tencent Launches Hy4, a Model Capable of Controlling a Computer
news.description: Hy4 understands images and can use software autonomously. Tencent ranks it as the second Chinese model behind Kimi K3.1 Pro, while acknowledging its limitations in advanced mathematics and complex image analysis.

news.title: Beijing Blocks SoftBank’s Acquisition of ABB’s Robotics Division
news.description: China vetoed SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division through its foreign investment oversight body. The decision highlights the growing strategic importance of industrial robots.

news.title: Anthropic signs its first licensing deal with the Associated Press
news.description: Anthropic has reached an agreement with the Associated Press allowing Claude to display midterm election results with their sources. The decision marks a shift in position after the company invoked fair use to collect news content.

news.title: U.S. Elections Threaten the Expansion of AI Data Centers
news.description: Democrats now control the U.S. House and Senate, while data centers influenced several local elections. The AI industry expects more regulation and a slowdown in new infrastructure.

news.title: Blue Origin Delays New Glenn’s Return to Flight Until January 2027
news.description: Jeff Bezos’s rocket is awaiting the reconstruction of its Cape Canaveral launch pad, destroyed by an explosion in May. Amazon is meanwhile using United Launch Alliance and Arianespace to deploy its satellite constellation.

news.title: AI Stocks Fall After the U.S. Elections
news.description: The Nasdaq fell 5.5%, while several chipmakers dropped more than 9% or by double digits. Wall Street fears a slowdown in data centers after the adoption of numerous local measures aimed at restricting them.

news.title: The AI Data Center Boom Draws Backlash After the U.S. Elections
news.description: Voters challenged the growth of AI-focused data centers. New restrictions could slow construction, increase costs and change how AI capacity is distributed.

news.title: 16 or 32 GB of RAM: Which Capacity Should You Choose for a Windows AI Laptop?
news.description: 16 GB is still enough for browsing, office work and cloud-based AI, while Windows 11 updates are improving the performance of computers with limited memory. The article details the use cases that genuinely justify 32 GB.

news.title: AI Agent Governance: Who Manages Access and Accountability?
news.description: New recommendations indicate that 71% of organizations give agents sensitive access, but only 35% use identity and access management. They call for designated owners, decision logging and testing of shutdown mechanisms.

news.title: Apple and Google Face Pressure Over More Than 400 Deepfake-Related Sites
news.description: More than 400 apps and sites linked to deepfakes that digitally undress people evaded Apple and Google’s controls. Hidden remote servers and ad-triggered features bypassed checks, while takedowns may not dismantle the abusive network.

news.title: Xiaomi Begins Rolling Out Android 17 HyperOS 4
news.description: HyperOS 4 will reach 82 Xiaomi, Redmi and Poco devices in three waves through December 2026. The update includes a redesigned interface, Super XiaoAi 2.0 with AI features, and performance and HDR improvements.
